title: Magnetism
standard_text: Magnets and magnetic fields; magnetic field lines around bar magnets; attraction and repulsion; the Earth's magnetic field and the compass; the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 10, Physics: Magnetism)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): magnets, magnetic poles, field lines, the Earth's magnetic field and compasses. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
key_sub: Field lines go from north to south outside a magnet.
body_html:
How to think about it

A magnet has a north and a south pole. A magnetic field is the region around a magnet where a magnetic material experiences a force. Field lines show the direction a compass needle points: from north to south outside the magnet; where lines are close together, the field is strong.

The Earth behaves like a giant bar magnet; a compass needle points to the magnetic north. The Earth's field protects us from charged particles from the Sun; near the poles these cause the aurora. A current in a wire also makes a magnetic field.

Example

What happens when two north poles are brought together?

Like poles

Answer: they repel

Example

Where is the field of a bar magnet strongest?

Look where the lines are closest.

Answer: at the poles

Common mistakes

  • Thinking field lines can cross.
  • Thinking all metals are magnetic.
  • Thinking the Earth's geographic and magnetic north are at the same place.

faq.q: Why does a compass point north?
faq.a: Its north pole is attracted to the Earth's magnetic pole in the north, which is a magnetic south pole.

items.q: The S pole of a magnet is brought near an unmagnetised iron nail. What happens?
c: The nail is attracted only to the S pole.
items.e: The nail becomes an induced magnet with the opposite pole nearest, so it is attracted to either pole.

items.q: The N pole of one magnet is brought near the S pole of another. What happens?
items.e: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

items.q: Is lead a magnetic material?
items.e: The magnetic materials are iron, steel, nickel and cobalt (and their alloys). Most other metals are non-magnetic.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a magnetic material?
items.e: Tin is not attracted by a magnet.

items.q: Which of these is a magnetic material?
items.e: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic.

items.q: How can a magnet be demagnetised?
c: by heating it strongly or hammering it, or by slowly withdrawing it from a solenoid carrying alternating current
by passing a direct current through a solenoid around it
by cooling it in a fridge
items.e: These disturb the alignment of the magnetic domains.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a magnetic material?
items.e: Silver is not attracted by a magnet.

items.q: How can a steel bar be magnetised using electricity?
c: Place it inside a solenoid and pass a direct current through the coil.
Pass alternating current through the bar.
items.e: The field of the solenoid magnetises the steel.

items.q: The N pole of a magnet is brought near an unmagnetised iron nail. What happens?
c: The nail is attracted only to the S pole.
items.e: The nail becomes an induced magnet with the opposite pole nearest, so it is attracted to either pole.

items.q: A freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest. Which way does its north pole point?
items.e: It is a north-seeking pole.

items.q: Which of these is a magnetic material?

items.q: The S pole of one magnet is brought near the S pole of another. What happens?

items.q: Why does a compass needle point north?
c: The North Pole is made of iron.
It lines up with the Earth's magnetic field.
It is attracted by the equator.
items.e: The Earth behaves like a giant bar magnet.

items.q: Which test shows that a metal bar is a magnet?
c: One end repels a pole of a known magnet.
items.e: Repulsion is the only sure test.

items.q: Is gold a magnetic material?

items.q: Is steel used to make temporary or permanent magnets?

items.q: Describe the field between two unlike poles (N facing S) placed close together.
c: nearly straight, parallel lines from N to S: a nearly uniform field
lines curving away from each other
items.e: Field lines go from N to S outside a magnet; closer lines mean a stronger field.

items.q: Two bar magnets are placed with N facing S a short distance apart. Where is the field most uniform?
c: in the gap between the poles
items.e: The lines are parallel there.

items.q: A magnet attracts both ends of a metal bar. What can you conclude?

items.e: A magnet would have one end repelled.

items.q: Which material is best for the core of a relay or electric bell: soft iron or steel?
items.e: Soft iron makes temporary magnets (easily magnetised and demagnetised); steel makes permanent magnets.

items.q: Where is the magnetic field of a bar magnet strongest?
c: in the middle of the magnet
near the poles, where the field lines are closest together
items.e: Field lines go from N to S outside a magnet; closer lines mean a stronger field.

items.q: What is a neutral point in a magnetic field?
c: a point with no magnets nearby
a point where the fields cancel, so the resultant field is zero
items.e: Field lines go from N to S outside a magnet; closer lines mean a stronger field.

items.q: What is a magnetic field?
c: the space inside a magnet only
a region in which a magnetic pole experiences a force
a region where electric charges feel a force
the path of an electric current
items.e: Field lines go from N to S outside a magnet; closer lines mean a stronger field.

items.q: Which material is best for a fridge door magnet: soft iron or steel?

items.q: Why are electromagnets in scrapyard cranes made with soft iron cores?

items.e: A steel core would stay magnetised.

items.q: Is soft iron used to make temporary or permanent magnets?

items.q: A plotting compass is placed east of a bar magnet's N pole (the magnet points north). Which way does the compass point?

items.q: Which material would make the best container to shield an instrument from magnetic fields?

items.q: Why should magnets not be dropped repeatedly on a hard floor?

items.q: In which direction do magnetic field lines point outside a bar magnet?

items.q: A paper clip hangs from a magnet. A second paper clip hangs from the first. Why?
